events.summary:
At 930 PM MST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Maricopa, or 12 miles southwest of Sun Lakes, moving northeast at 30
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Phoenix, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Tempe, Sun Lakes, Maricopa,
Chandler Fashion Center Mall, Arizona Mills Mall, Chandler City
Hall, Tumbleweed Park, South Mountain Park, Arizona State
University, Fiesta Mall, Bapchule, Tempe Marketplace, South
Phoenix, Sky Harbor Airport and Gilbert City Hall.

This includes the following highways...
AZ Route 87 between mile markers 158 and 167. AZ Route 202 near mile
marker 1...and between mile markers 10 and 11...and between mile
markers 2 and 3...and between mile markers 37 and 39...and near mile
marker 4...and near mile marker 40. AZ Route 101 between mile markers
51 and 60. US Highway 60 between mile markers 173 and 182. AZ
Interstate 17 between mile markers 195 and 197. AZ Route 51 between
mile markers 1 and 5. AZ Interstate 10 between mile markers 145 and
148...and between mile markers 149 and 153. AZ Route 238 between mile
markers 42 and 44. AZ Route 347 between mile markers 174 and 183.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Castle Country; San Rafael Swell
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country and San Rafael Swell.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A late season surge of tropical moisture will bring widespread
moderate to at times heavy rainfall across much of eastern Utah
beginning Wednesday afternoon, and continuing through Thursday.
Local rainfall totals in excess of 2 inches are expected through
Thursday evening.
- All normally dry washes, small streams and mainstem rivers will
see elevated flows from this excessive rainfall, with periods of
heavier rainfall resulting in flash flooding. Backcountry roads
may become impassable due to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Southwest San Juan Mountains; Four Corners/Upper Dolores River; Animas River Basin; San Juan River Basin; Southeast Utah; Arches/Grand Flat; La Sal and Abajo Mountains; Canyonlands/Natural Bridges
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and Utah,
including the following areas, Arches/Grand Flat,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recent burn scars and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong thunderstorms capable of producing heavy rain could
develop Wednesday and Thursday afternoons. Widespread moderate to
heavy rainfall will also occur from a surge of tropical moisture
arriving tomorrow and lingering through Friday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
